Losses in the petrochemicals business narrowed to Rs 22 crore from Rs 299 crore a year earlier. There will be no fresh mainboard IPO launches, although several companies that raised funds in late October are preparing for their stock market debuts. Vedant Poly Fabs, a small and medium enterprise (SME), will be the only new company opening its IPO next week. Meanwhile, six companies whose public issues are currently open, including mainboard player Bombay Coated & Special Steels, are scheduled to list on the exchanges during the week. The slowdown follows a busy October for India's primary market, highlighted by Jio Platforms ' Rs 30,188 crore IPO, the largest in the country's history. Mukesh Ambani-led Jio made its stock market debut on October 28 at Rs 1,358, a premium of 21.36% over its issue price of Rs 1,119. Your customers haven't changed, and your operations remain the same, but the rules of the game have. This is where the relationship between regulation and free markets becomes complicated. Free markets thrive on competition, innovation and commercial freedom. Regulation, on the other hand, is essential to protect consumers, prevent the misuse of market power and build trust. The challenge begins when intervention goes beyond correcting market failures and starts altering the economic incentives that make businesses viable. A sudden change in these economics can affect earnings visibility, business expansion and investor sentiment.
